sources.mcu_revision: every DS12110 citation in this note is Rev 8 (April 2021), revision V electrical chapter (section 7; the LCSC copy is byte-identical), except the two design limits labelled as read from Rev 11 Table 109 in round 14 (the 6.0 V FT cap and the 4.0 V ADC-mode maximum; R5-MCU-04 obligation, Inference); Rev 11 and RM0433 were not re-read in round 19 (R19-MCU-02)

port_states.reset_boot: GPS/radio/AUX ports (J410/J420/J440, electrically identical, D-R19-14) powered directly by PORT_4V8 whenever the battery path is on (off on USB-only power); their UARTs reach FT digital MCU pins through 1 kohm and a ground-only ESD clamp. Keep direct UART RX internal pulls disabled throughout operation; the FT operating pull-off condition is the relevant I/O supply + 0.3 V. Camera EN100k/OE10k pulldowns retain power/isolation default-off.
port_states.off_external_uart_active: GPS/radio/AUX ports have no powered-off isolation. An externally powered module can inject through the kept 1 kohm into an unpowered MCU; no self-powered GPS/radio with the board off. The SD card remains on main3V3, with CS held high by R460 (10 kohm) at reset.
port_states.startup: Port UART TX (J410 PD8 USART3, J420 PB13 UART5, J440 PC6 USART6): select the TX alternate function (idle high) only while PA4 LOGIC_SOURCE_ST reads low after a settling delay (U11 ST low = IN2 = RAW_PROTECTED, the battery path that powers PORT_4V8; ST high = IN1 = USB or no valid input; TI SLVSEA3F Table 9-3 p. 18, p. 21); while PA4 reads high the modules may be unpowered (USB-only), so PD8 / PB13 / PC6 stay in analog mode, no pull (R19-MCU-01). Camera: EN high, verified rail settling, RX pull-up and TX idle-high, then OE high. SD_CS high before SPI3 AF6 configuration.
port_states.shutdown_shedding: GPS/radio/AUX port supply cannot be switched or power-cycled by firmware. When PA4 rises or the PA6 VLOGIC watchdog trips, park PD8 / PB13 / PC6 in analog mode, no pull (R19-MCU-01). Stop UARTs and SD/QSPI writes, disable camera OE then EN, lower MCU clock, extinguish LEDs/buzzer. Faulted cards must not block safety/flight tasks.
port_states.port_device_backfeed: Always-on GPS/radio/AUX port power pins directly back-feed PORT_4V8; U401/U400 can then feed RAW_PROTECTED/VLOGIC (Inference). The retained camera TPS2553 blocks reverse current when disabled, but an enabled part trips only beyond95-190mV after3-7ms (TI SLVS841G section6.5p7); UART isolation does not qualify its power pin. J400 has no state sensor, so back-feed can hide switch opening. Connect the e-match only with no USB/self-powered port source attached; bench USB with pack disconnected or e-match disconnected. No firmware mitigation replaces this restriction.

arming_policy.decision: owner single screw switch, 2026-10-28; J124 and its ARM-link fuse removed
arming_policy.hardware: J400 is the pad power/arming device, connected to U9 EN with no switch-state sensor. Q120/Q121 feed RAW_ACT directly to R134 and R132. PC1 independently enables Q122 through R122; PE4 separately drives Q124. Both MCU controls default off in reset.
arming_policy.pad: Turn the screw switch on last and off first, only with the vehicle on the pad / rail. GPS, telemetry and IMU pad checks occur on the rail.
arming_policy.bench: Use USB with the pack disconnected, or disconnect the e-match. Connect the e-match only with no USB or self-powered port back-feed source attached.
arming_policy.limits: No physical ARM break while powered; a back-feed source can keep logic powered with J400 open. Continuity and ARM1_SENSE measure the firing return and RAW_ACT bus, not a separate ARM-link state.

fire_timing.basis: GAP-5; DS12110 Rev 8 Table 146 p. 238: LSI 29.4-33.6 kHz at TJ -40 to 125 C; firmware obligations, not implemented
fire_timing.refresh_contract: No IWDG refresh from prefire through firing until physical firing current has ended (including tail); then require the SAFETY pass and refeed within 5ms. A failed safety task never refreshes.

r10_firmware_obligations: Build a new reviewed binding through the assembly_binding design process; never substitute a board hash into the R1 chain.

Port UARTs (D-R19-14): J410 USART3 PD8 TX/PD9 RX AF7 (DS12110 Rev 8 Table 13 p. 94), J420 UART5 PB13 TX/PB12 RX AF14 (Rev 8 Table 11 p. 91), J440 USART6 PC6 TX/PC7 RX AF7 (Rev 8 Table 12 p. 92); the same cites as pin_table.tsv rows 55-56, 51-52 and 63-64.

Configurable port map (D-R19-14, owner 2026-10-30): J410, J420 and J440 are electrically identical (pin 1 PORT_4V8, 2 GND, 3 board TXO, 4 board RXI; 1 kohm series, ground-only ESD clamp, 100 nF + 22 uF local supply), so the GPS and the radio may each be wired to any of the three. Firmware maps each device to a port UART (baud, protocol and receive handling follow the device, not the port); default GPS J410 (USART3), radio J420 (UART5), J440 AUX spare (USART6). The camera port J9 is not part of the set (5.4 V supply, reversed TX/RX order, isolated UART). The three ports share PORT_4V8: the spare port (AUX by default) may draw up to 100 mA at 4.8 V beyond the GPS 150 mA and radio 300 mA allocations (U401 thermal floor: junction <= 125 C at the 70 C bay with the inferred 110 C/W theta-JA, Inference; parts_budget.json). A port with no mapped device keeps its USART disabled and both pins in analog mode, no pull, so an open RX never floats as a digital input (R20-MCU-03).

Camera UART7 PE8 TX/PE7 RX AF7 without flow control. UART5/USART6 and USART3 on PD8/PD9 are separate from the loader USART interfaces (AN2606 Rev64 Table119 pp277-280: no UART5, PB12 or PB13; the loader USART3 is PB10/PB11 only).

Re-mapped loader pins (AN2606 Rev64 Table119 pp279-280; pin_table an2606_t119_loader_role): PA4 / PA5 / PA6 are SPI1 NSS / SCK / MISO and PE11 / PE12 SPI4 NSS / SCK. In the ROM loader PA6 is driven push-pull into the VLOGIC_SENSE divider only (<= 0.36 mA) and PE11 is an input that R431 holds low (camera port off); before a loader jump drive camera EN/OE low, PC1/PE4 low and SD_CS high. PC11 is loader SPI3_MISO output; R460 keeps the card deselected.

Always-on GPS/radio/AUX ports have no FAULT/EN/OE GPIOs; PD10/PD14/PD15/PE15 are NC/analog. EXTI12 CAM_FAULT_N (PE12); EXTI4 LOGIC_SOURCE_ST (PA4) and EXTI5 BAT_FAULT_N (PA5), swapped for routing (D-R2-09); EXTI6 USB_FAULT_N (PD6), EXTI8 VBUS_SENSE (PC8). AUD-4 removes PULLPIN; PC13 is NC. One port per EXTI line; lines5/6/8 share EXTI9_5 and line12 uses EXTI15_10, so each handler checks its pending bit. PE1 IMU_INT1 is on EXTI1 (free on R10; R6-MCU-01): configure PE1 as an input with the internal pull-down and take the roll-loop data-ready interrupt on it; U4 INT1 is push-pull and active high by default (IF_CFG PP_OD = 0, H_LACTIVE = 0 on the fitted ISM6HG256X and the alternate LSM6DSV320X: DS15034 / DS14623 Rev 1 p. 60), so no pull-up is wanted. EXTI1 has its own vector.

PE4 (U1.3, net PYRO1_GATE_N; the _N is historical) is the ACTIVE-HIGH fire command: PE4 high turns Q124 on. Write its output data low before output mode and keep it low except during a permitted fire (R18-MCU-03). R123 2k (R18-MCU-01) and R127 1k hold Q122 / Q124 off against a 30-50 kOhm internal pull-up; never enable a PC1 or PE4 pull-up, and never route RTC_TAMP3 or WKUP5 to PC1. PC1 ACT_EN_MCU and PE4 pyro gate low before GPIO configuration, port shutdown, ROM-loader entry or reset. PC1 is the independent Q120/Q121 enable through R122, not a sentinel. Keep sentinel pins PE3/PE5/PE6/PC4 without nets and in analog mode (their reset state), never driven: every no-net pin, the sentinels included, stays analog (R5-MCU-03). PA15 is the one no-net pin whose reset state is NOT analog (R7-MCU-01): it resets to JTDI with the internal pull-up (STM32H743 debug-pin reset state, DS12110 / RM0433 as the reviewer read it, not re-read here: Inference), so set PA15 to analog mode with no pull explicitly at start-up; "reset state" wording applies only to the other no-net pins.

GAP-5: keep the independent safety task and IWDG divide-by-4 (PR register 0) / RLR 239 (960 LSI cycles): 30ms nominal, 28.571-32.653ms at LSI 33.6-29.4kHz (DS12110 Rev 8 Table 146 p. 238, TJ -40 to 125 C). Never refresh from prefire through firing until physical firing current has ended (including tail); require the postfire SAFETY pass and refeed within 5ms. Limit NORMAL PHYSICAL igniter current, including the actual gate-discharge tail, to 20ms; a 20ms GPIO-high command alone is insufficient. Worst-fault physical current is bounded by 32.653ms watchdog +0.2ms prefire/synchronization +0.5ms reset HiZ +1.5ms actual gate-current tail =34.853ms, within the 36ms contract (Calculation on allocations: the 0.2 / 0.5 / 1.5 ms need bench tests, and the 1.5 ms covers a 0.74 ms gate-discharge model whose 0.4 V off criterion and hot gate charge are Inference; parts_budget.json pyro_fault_GAP5). These are firmware and bench obligations, not implemented. Never fire before launch is detected using accelerometer and barometer. On the ground continuity / bus readings are hard refusals; in flight they are logged and annunciated and never veto a fire. The screw switch is the pad arming device; no separate ARM plug or ARM-link state exists.

F6 / FMEA F-1: the first SERVO1-4 output after reset is neutral 1520us, with a command within 50ms. GAP-5 uses the 960-LSI-cycle IWDG period specified above; only the SAFETY task may refresh it, subject to the no-refresh firing interval. A ROM-loader jump is allowed only before IWDG starts: it cannot be stopped afterward; keep both firing controls low.

D-SS-04 / AUD-3: hold BOTH PC1 ACT_EN_MCU and PE4 low for passive cold screening. After a prior load-switch enable, wait at least 1s and verify RAW_ACT discharged / ACT_GATE off before classifying readings. Bench-qualify passive low/healthy/open bands, leakage and unexpected powered-bus readings using parts_qualification.md; any ground fault is a hard refusal BEFORE PC1 enable, especially a failed-short Q124. Only after a valid passive check may PC1 go high, with PE4 still low for at least 100ms before powered-bus checks or any permitted fire. This settling wait is not the no-refresh firing interval; in-flight sense readings never veto fire.

J122 DB1255pos pins1-4SERVO1-4_OUT,pin5GND signal reference; servo positive and motor return direct to pack. Board cannot cut servo power; qualify neutral-on-reset and measured shared return. J400 DB1252pos is power/arming switch; J9/J410/J420/J440 DB1254pos unkeyed, explicit per-pin power/GND/UART legends and end-to-end harness check; clamps28-16AWG with qualified ferrules/splices for thinner module leads.
Maximum normal-flight MCU clock200MHz for the retained-load budget. Firmware not implemented.

F6 battery-break response (always-on port owner decision2026-10-28): C84 plus firmware shedding, no hardware U400 cutoff and no GPS/radio switches. Use PA6 ADC12_INP3 watchdog on ADC1/2. Ports-on ride-through includes the always-on GPS/radio, the 100 mA AUX allowance and the card allocation; no software power cutoff can be credited. Bench-verify detection latency, selected-card current, camera current decay and retained load. Loaded battery-break continuity is not guaranteed.

On shedding stop SD and QSPI writes immediately without a blocking flush, stop UARTs, lower camera OE then EN, lower MCU clock, extinguish LEDs/buzzer; retain IMU/barometer/flight state and safety. The SD card may stay busy and powered after host clocks stop; budget its<=200mA write allocation until its actual current falls. No in-flight wait for filesystem/card completion.

Camera TPS2553 FAULT deglitch is3-11ms, turn-off up to3ms (TI SLVS841G p7). FAULT is not battery-break detection. GPS/radio/AUX ports rely on shared LDO/buck current and thermal limits; a short can remove all three port loads, with no independent fault flag or firmware recovery power-cycle.

On VLOGIC undervoltage/shutdown drop camera EN/OE and park PD8 / PB13 / PC6 in analog mode, no pull; the GPS/radio/AUX ports stay powered whenever the battery path is on (firmware cannot switch them; off on USB-only power). J400 has no state sensor; retain the no-self-powered-port/e-match restriction. Direct port UARTs are FT digital inputs only, RX pulls always disabled; a device on J410 / J420 / J440 must drive its TX high at no more than 3.6 V, because PORT_4V8 can rise tens of ms before 3V3 (the 470 nF U11 soft-start (C85) slews VLOGIC at about 166–196 V/s after its settling time, TI SLVSEA3F Table 9-1 p. 13 scaled to 470 nF, and U2 (AP63203) starts at 3.3–3.7 V with a 4 ms soft-start, Diodes DS41326 p. 5, so 3V3 regulates about 21–26 ms into the slew; Calculation / Inference: the table is scaled linearly and the settling time is not quantified; measure the PORT_4V8-to-3V3 lag on first articles) and an FT pin allows only 4.0 V while VDD = 0 (DS12110 Rev 8 Table 119 p. 212; R20-MCU-02). ST DS12110 Rev 8 Table 122 note 3 p. 215 / Table 157 note 7 p. 247 requires pulls off above Min(VDD, VDDA, VDD33USB) + 0.3 V in operation; Table 119 note 4 p. 213 gives a separate 4 V absolute-stress condition. No powered-off isolation or positive injected current allowance.

PC14 drives the buzzer gate through R162 1 kOhm: VBAT-domain PC13/PC14/PC15 are characterised at +/-3 mA only (DS12110 Rev 8 Table 159 p. 249); GPIO speed low (2 MHz limit, Rev 8 Table 160 note 2 p. 251), as pin_table.tsv row 8.

Switch-chatter immunity is hardware only (C87 220 nF, R19-REQ-02 / D-R19-10 / D-R20-11 / D-R24-19 / D-R25-01 / D-R26-03): a single J400 drop-out shorter than 10.3/20.1/26.0 ms worst case (19/33/41 ms nominal) at 6.0/7.4/8.4 V, about 8.1 ms (8.07 ms) at the fire budget four-stall BAT_IN of 5.71 V (5.713 V, parts_budget.json, with the 100 mA AUX allowance; R26-TRI-02) and 6.3 ms at 5.5 V cannot trip U9 (Calculation / Inference, R20-SAF-04 / R24-TRI-02: 297 kOhm x 0.72 x 220 nF from EN 1.401 V at 6.0 V (1 % divider, 0.1 uA EN leakage out of the node and D402's 50 nA at J400.2) falling to 1.116 V with the same leakages on R81, D402's through R165; TPS25947 SLVSFC9C p. 9 EN thresholds and leakage, Infineon ESD103 Rev 1.3 leakage; Inference: C87's 0.72 x minimum takes its X7R DC-bias loss as at most 6 % without the maker's curve (D-R19-10), and the 5.71 V point is the fire budget's, whose hot Q124 factor is inferred). Repeated drop-outs add up (R25-TRI-01): the worst-corner trip fraction of periodic chatter falls from 19.6 % at 0.1 ms drop-outs to 14.8 % at 4 ms and 4.5 % at 8 ms (5.71 V) and from 24.3 % to 8.3 % at 9.9 ms (6.0 V); 19.7 / 24.4 % is only the fast-chatter limit, and these fractions are guidance only. REQUIREMENTS F6 bench acceptance: record the J400 contact state at 10 kS/s or faster under flight-level vibration and pass only if the total open time in every sliding 100 ms window is under 7 ms and U9 stays on for the whole run at 5.71 V (worst-corner limit 7.50 ms per 100 ms window at 5.71 V, a 0.50 ms margin over the 7 ms line, which holds down to 5.65 V; 5.87 ms at 5.5 V, 9.59 ms at 6.0 V). The worst admissible train is one open block per 100 ms placed late in the window (exchange argument: C(O(v)) - O(C(v)) = (1 - a)(1 - b)(vc - vo) > 0): at the corner it trips U9 at 7.50 ms at 5.71 V (7.63 ms at 5.73 V), and at the 7 ms pass line it holds EN at 1.1295 V at 5.71 V (1.1330 V at 5.73 V) against 1.116 V (Calculation / Inference, R26-TRI-03: the same EN model). A switch that fails may still pass on a replay of its recorded contact waveform through the worst-corner EN model. Re-size C87 (BOM only, same land) if a real switch cannot meet it; keep it separate from battery-lead-break ride-through. A longer drop-out reboots the board after a 30-130 ms EN turn-on delay (the same model over C87 0.72-1.27 x). Resume flight state from live evidence after reset.

Radio uplink cannot arm or fire; LR900-F band is 890-915 MHz: use manual channels 12-25 (902-915 MHz) or a maker-confirmed FHSS set inside 902-928 MHz; qualify installed maximum-power radio/GPS immunity.

PC14 buzzer GPIO-toggled; PC13, PE10 and PE0 remain NC (AUD-4 removes the pull-pin). Audit2: PC0 PYRO1_CONT and PC5 ARM1_SENSE directly read their retained split dividers and10nF filters, withoutR168/R170 tails; duplicate bus bank/PB0 removed. Sensor functions unchanged.

UART start-up: camera retains U12 isolation and OE pull-down; before camera OE goes high, RX PE7 pull-up and TX PE8 idle-high. The three port UARTs connect directly through 1 kohm; PD9/PB12/PC7 are digital AF inputs with internal pulls always disabled; PD8/PB13/PC6 take their TX alternate function (idle high) only while PA4 LOGIC_SOURCE_ST reads low after a settling delay (U11 ST low = IN2 = RAW_PROTECTED, the battery path that powers PORT_4V8; ST high = IN1 = USB or no valid input; TI SLVSEA3F Table 9-3 p. 18, p. 21), and return to analog mode, no pull when PA4 rises or the PA6 watchdog trips: on USB-only power the port modules are unpowered, so the MCU cannot back-feed a module through the 1 kohm (R19-MCU-01). Never connect a self-powered port module with the board off; measure endpoint TX levels.

Per-sense ADC instances: PC0 PYRO1_CONT ADC123_INP10, PA6 VLOGIC_SENSE ADC12_INP3, PC5 ARM1_SENSE ADC12_INP8 (sole RAW_ACT bus reading), PB1 CAM_5V_SENSE ADC12_INP5. PB0 and PC3_C are NC/analog (R18-REQ-08 removes the V3V3_SENSE divider R62/R63: it read 3V3 against VREF+ = 3V3A from the same rail); read VDDA from VREFINT (VREFIN_CAL, DS12110 Rev 8 Tables 127-128 pp. 218-219) and 3V3 from the internal VBAT/4 bridge (VBAT tied to 3V3; Rev 8 Table 192 p. 293, ratio error +/-10%) on ADC3, as pin_table.tsv row 18. Delete duplicate RAW_ACT_SENSE readings and thresholds. Ground continuity and sole bus readings remain hard refusals; in flight neither vetoes fire. PA6 watchdog uses ADC1/2.

microSD J430 locking hinge, no card-detect: SPI3 AF6 PC10 SCK/PC11 MISO/PC12 MOSI, PD0 software CS. CS high before GPIO/AF setup; >= 74 clocks with CS/MOSI high at 100-400 kHz, then CMD0; run at <= 25 MHz. The R460-R464 (10 kohm) pull-ups to 3V3 and the 3V3 bypass are physical. Select and bench-qualify a card with <= 200 mA write and <= 30 mA idle; keep locked during flight, insert/remove only off with board out.

F5: nominal whole-flight storage spans retained QSPI plus secondary removable microSD, with adequate bounded buffering and at least25% measured throughput margin. No requirement that a whole flight fit16MB QSPI alone. A missing/faulted/full/slow card or corrupt filesystem never delays control, safety, watchdog or fire. Use nonblocking bounded transfers and preallocated files; drop secondary SD records only as fault/overload fallback, not the normal capacity plan. Power loss may corrupt the card; no blocking flush during F6 or firing.
Audit2 item16: keep both LEDs dark from arming to landing until the installed opaque U5 cover passes LED-toggle/ambient-light checkout; the CAD cannot certify the cover.

Selected MJG J-Tek LEAD-FREE maker all-fire0.75A times1.5 gives1.125A current criterion; the maker0.5s test does not certify20ms. Retain R1342ohm, normal physical20ms/fault36ms and qualify selected-lot20ms firing/source/harness/charge before flight.

No-net U1 pins (R4-MCU-04): every U1 pin with no net stays in analog mode (the reset state) and is never configured as an output; the K-loader no-net pins (pin_table an2606_t119_loader_role) are never outputs, so a ROM-loader drive or a stray configuration cannot reach copper.

LSE (R5-MCU-02): keep RCC_BDCR.LSEON = 0 and never set up the backup domain for the LSE: PC14 is OSC32_IN and drives BUZZ_DRV through R162, and VBAT is tied to 3V3, so a stray LSEON persists across NRST.

VBUS_SENSE (R5-MCU-05): PC8 = VBUS / 2 (R9 1 kOhm / R110 1 kOhm); at 4.4 V VBUS the node is 2.20 V, below VIH = 0.7 x VDD = 2.31 V, so VBUS detection needs VBUS >= 4.62 V at VDD 3.3 V. A low PC8 is not proof of no USB: never use it as the sole input to a safety decision.

Audit2 direct PC0/PC5 filtered ADCs retain single-resistor protection; duplicate PB0 bank andR168/R170 tails are removed. Other unprotected sense faults (R5-MCU-04): PA6 VLOGIC_SENSE (shorted R60 puts VLOGIC on an FT_a pin; positive injection allowance 0 mA (DS12110 Rev 8 Table 120 note 3 p. 213). Rev 8 Table 119 pp. 212-213 (notes 3-4) gives the FT ceiling Min(VDD, VDDA, VDD33USB, VBAT) + 4.0 V with pulls disabled above 4 V and 4.0 V on TT pins; the 4.0 V ADC-mode maximum and the 6.0 V FT cap were read from Rev 11 Table 109 in round 14 and are kept as design limits (Inference: not in Rev 8, Rev 11 not re-read)) and PB1 CAM_5V_SENSE (open R105 puts CAM_5V on a TT_u pin through R104 10 kOhm, limit 4.0 V); single-fault pin-damage cases recorded in parts_qualification.md, no firmware mitigation.

Trace (R6-MCU-03): never enable synchronous trace (PE2 TRACECLK, PC1 TRACED0, PE4 TRACED1) in any debug configuration: PC1 enables the load switch and PE4 is the pyro gate (PYRO1_GATE); trace would drive both firing controls. After PC1 and PE4 are configured as low outputs, lock PC1 with GPIOC_LCKR and PE4 with GPIOE_LCKR (the locks hold until the next reset), then read both registers back: bit 16 (LCKK) and the pin lock bit (PC1 bit 1, PE4 bit 4) must read 1, and the firmware refuses to arm otherwise (D-SS-02 / R7-MCU-02). A locked pin's output data can still be written, its configuration cannot: in a loader-jump sequence PC1 and PE4 stay locked low outputs, because GPIOC / GPIOE resets (RCC_AHB4RSTR) clear the locks and only R123 / R127 then hold the controls off. R10 locks PC1 and PE4: PE3 / PE5 / PE6 are analog sentinels, PE12 is the CAM_FAULT_N input and PE13 / PE14 are NC. Disconnect the e-match before connecting a trace-capable debugger session: whether the DBGMCU trace pin assignment overrides the GPIO configuration (and the lock) on the H743 is not checked (Inference; R7-SAF-03).

UART break storm: camera retains the TXU0202 input pull-down and can report a continuous break if enabled while unplugged. Direct port UARTs (GPS/radio/AUX) can float/noise when unplugged. Receive by DMA/IDLE with bounded error handling; mask FE/NE/ORE per-frame storms and disable the affected UART after a bounded error threshold. Port modules cannot be isolated or power-cycled in software; camera OE may be lowered.

Trace override bench step (R8-SAF-01 / R9-MCU-01): no e-match connected. Use a debugger-supported STM32H743 synchronous 4-bit ETM setup; RM0433 Rev8 pp3209/543 uses DBGMCU_CR at 0x5C001004 bit20 TRACECLKEN (CMSIS DBGMCU_CR_DBG_TRACECKEN), not TRACE_IOEN or TRACE_MODE. With QSPI idle, set PE2 AF0 TRACECLK; keep PC1 and PE4 locked low GPIO outputs, not trace alternate functions. Read back both GPIOC_LCKR and GPIOE_LCKR: LCKK bit16 plus PC1 bit1 / PE4 bit4 must remain set. Verify the debugger did not reset GPIOC/GPIOE or clear either lock. Observe a running PE2 trace clock before quiet PC1 / PE4 / TP122 counts as evidence; absent clock or lost lock invalidates the test. If either control toggles with valid clock/locks, enforce trace-clock disable and readback before arming and report it (override behavior remains Inference until measured).

W25Q128JV (R6-MCU-04): set the QE bit in status register 2 before QSPI quad mode is used; no blocking flash erase in flight: pre-erase before flight or use erase-suspend, so that the GAP-5 28.571ms minimum IWDG period holds (W25Q128JV Rev I AC characteristics, read in round 7: 4 KB sector erase 45 ms typical / 400 ms maximum, 32 KB block 120 / 1,600 ms, 64 KB block 150 / 2,000 ms, erase-suspend latency tSUS 20 us). The pad ring buffer must be erased in erase-suspend slices or sized for a single pre-erase before arming; erase time is added to the F5 timing-margin statement. This is an open firmware design obligation (R7-MCU-04).

IMU (R6-MCU-05, D-R19-11): U4 is fitted as the ISM6HG256X (JLC C51931514); the LSM6DSV320X is the second-fallback alternate (needs part fields, BOM and CPL regenerated: ORDERING 8.1) on the same land with the same pins and axis directions (DS15034 Rev 1 Figure 5 p. 9 and Table 2 p. 11; DS14623 Rev 1 p. 9). WHO_AM_I reads 0x73 on both (p. 66), so it cannot identify the part. Their high-g full-scale codes differ (FS_XL_HG, Table 150 p. 93 of both: ISM6HG256X 100 = +/-256 g and 011 reserved; LSM6DSV320X 011 = +/-256 g and 100 = +/-320 g): use only 001 (+/-64 g) or 010 (+/-128 g), which mean the same on both and meet F2. IMU SPI clock <= 10 MHz (DS15034 p. 17); ignore gyro data for 40 ms after an IMU power-up (Ton, DS15034 p. 15).

VREFBUF (R19-MCU-04): VREF+ (U1.20) is tied to VDDA (U1.21) on 3V3A (DS12110 Rev 8 Figure 95 p. 286). Keep VREFBUF_CSR at its reset value (ENVR = 0, HIZ = 1 per the ST SVD) and never write it: never enable the buffer (no HAL_SYSCFG_EnableVREFBUF) and never clear HIZ, since ENVR = 0 with HIZ = 0 pulls VREF+ to VSSA and would load 3V3A (VDDA, U4, U5) through R164 (RM0433 mode table as quoted on the ST community forum; Inference, R20-MCU-01). Scale ADC readings from VREFINT: an enabled buffer would drive its 1.5-2.5 V output (Table 189 p. 291, 4 mA static load) against 3V3A. Table 9 note 7 p. 88 requires the buffer kept disabled where VREF+ is tied to VDDA inside the package; applying it to this board-level tie is an Inference (RM0433 not re-read).

R23 firmware rule 1, launch (R23-SAFETY-07): the fire path needs LIFTOFF from the accelerometer AND a barometric altitude gain (LAUNCH_CORROBORATED), as AGENTS §2.1 requires. There is no inertial-only fire path on R10. With the barometer invalid, the primary channel does not fire and the independent Blue Jay covers recovery. FMEA F-6's accelerometer-only latch is not enough on R10.

R23 firmware rule 2, cold screen after every power-up or reset (R23-SAFETY-09): wait at least 1 s, and verify that RAW_ACT has discharged and ACT_GATE is off, before classifying. This covers both U9 variants.

R23 firmware rule 3, QSPI_IO2 / PE4 bridge (R23-SAFETY-08 (1); verified Minor by round23_safety_severity_check.md). Physics: Q124's gate capacitor is C126, 220 nF, not C128 (100 nF, on the drain); the gate time constant is about 47–58 µs over C126's ±10 % (53 µs nominal; Calculation, driver resistances Inference); a steady IO2-against-PE4 fight with the MCU driving IO2 high puts 1.19–1.98 V on the gate and fires the match after about 0.55 ms in all but one modelled corner; page-program logging at a QSPI clock of 25 MHz or more stays at most 6 mA RMS, at least 50× below the 0.30 A no-fire (Calculation / Simulation; driver resistances, flash drive, the AON7524 sub-amp curve and the match thermal model are Inference); firing needs a sustained IO2-high pattern. Ground refusal: before PC1 goes high, run a QSPI quad read-verify of a known pattern, and refuse on any mismatch: the bridge corrupts quad reads. QSPI use while PC1 is high: PE2 stays in its QSPI alternate function, never a GPIO driven high; no memory-mapped or parked quad reads; no long all-ones writes at a low clock; the flash output drive is not at 100 %. Cold screen: during part of the passive cold screen, run sustained QSPI traffic and toggle PC14 and the servo PWM; refuse if CONT or BUS moves out of band. First article, before first power and coating: inspect U1 pins 1–5 for bridges, and, with the board unpowered (pack and USB disconnected), meter U3.3 (QSPI_IO2) to R127.1 (the PE4 gate network) in resistance mode, both polarities: an intact board reads above 0.9 kΩ, or open, both ways (red lead on R127.1: a diode drop plus about 0.91 kΩ through the U1 / U3 input clamps; reversed: open or slowly rising); a continuity beep or under 100 Ω in either polarity is a bridge: reject (0.91 kΩ is R127's 1 kΩ in parallel with R126 + R128, Calculation; the meter's reading through the clamps is an Inference).

R23 firmware rule 4, bus voltage (R23-SAFETY-05): on the ground, after PC1 goes high and a 100 ms settle, the powered BUS must read at least 0.96 × the pack voltage derived from VLOGIC_SENSE, else refuse (this catches Q120 left off and the bus fed through its body diode). Qualify the band on first articles. Verified Minor: four stalls give 1.128 / 1.063 A (0.7 / 1.0 V drop: AONR21357 VSD typical / maximum at 1 A, p. 2; Calculation / Inference: the fire budget's hot Q124 factor is inferred), 0.93–1.01× the 1.125 A floor but at least 1.39× the maker's 0.75 A all-fire and at least 1.04× its 1.00 A recommended minimum. A first-order thermal model fires the match in 4–5 ms, inside the 20 ms pulse (Inference). At first article, before coating, with PC1 high and a dummy load in J121: ACT_GATE at R120.2 / C120.2, against Q120's source at R120.1, must settle at |VGS| of at least 4.5 V (a Q120 gate cut off from R121 sits near 0 V), and during the dummy-load fire BAT_IN − RAW_ACT above 0.2 V fails the board (R23-SAFETY-05's criterion: Q120's body diode adds 0.7–1.0 V). Since D-R24-02 each gate drive has a second barrel (Q120 (16.2, 73.3) + (15.4, 72.85), Q121 (11.14, 71.7) + (11.74, 72.3)): leaving Q120 off this way takes two opens (D-R24-19).

R23 firmware rule 5, PC1 source rule (R23-SAFETY-02 (4)): PC1 may go high only while PA4 reads low (U11 on the battery path, so U9 and J400 are on) and VBUS_SENSE does not contradict it. R91.1 and U1.28 each have a second via since D-R24-08 (no single point; the D-R22-02 entries are gone), and the rule stays an extra barrier, not a guarantee.

R23 firmware rule 6, LANDED (R23-SAFETY-04, R23-REQUIREMENTS-06): use FMEA 7.4'.9's criteria with a T_min floor. Then PE4 and PC1 go low and stay latched until power-off; PC1 never re-enables in the same power session. The IWDG keeps being serviced until power-off. The GPS and radio keep beaconing position: the ports are always on, so FMEA F-8's "GNSS off" does not apply to R10; park the GNSS UART instead if power must be shed. The locator tone sounds; logging stops or drops to 1 Hz.

R23 firmware rule 7, PA5 (R23-POWER-04): PA5 low also means U9 is blocking reverse current (SLVSFC9C Table 7-3 p38). Treat it as a U9 fault only when it stays low longer than a qualified time with RAW_PROTECTED collapsed. Rate-limit EXTI5, and never reset or refuse readiness on one pulse. PA4 during U11's own reverse blocking is unstated (Inference): deglitch PA4 before re-enabling the port UARTs.

R23 firmware rule 8, PA6 trip and hold-up (R23-POWER-01): the PA6 trip window is VLOGIC about 4.8–5.2 V (PA6 0.44–0.47 V): above U9's 4.80 V BAT_IN turn-off corner (D402's 50 nA included, D-R24-19; the PA6 lower edge 0.44 V x 11 = 4.84 V stays above it) and below the four-stall-plus-fire corner: BAT_IN 5.71 V with a healthy match (the fire budget's four-stall point, which includes the 1.28 A fire current), 5.55–5.56 V with the match shorted and 5.50 V with the match and leads shorted; VLOGIC is 0.09–0.16 V lower (fire_current_GAP1 model, Calculation / Inference: its hot Q124 factor is inferred; R26-TRI-04, D-R26-03). The window is to be qualified with the divider and ADC tolerances. Hold-up after the trip is 0.103–0.164 ms with all ports on and 0.291–0.430 ms with the camera off / shed, 0.22–0.31 of the break-to-3.8 V hold-up (Calculation / Inference, D-R25-02: constant power at 300.8 µF to 3.8 V from VLOGIC 4.84–5.17 V, the PA6 0.44–0.47 V window; the shortest at the window's lower edge; the loads are the budget's allocations, and C84 has no cold-capacitance factor).

R23 firmware rule 9, pad readiness. Pack (R23-REQUIREMENTS-07): firmware reads PA6, and PC5 after the cold screen. It telemeters the pack voltage and refuses the pad READY state below 7.4 V plus the measured PA6 divider error. Temperature (R23-MECHANICS-03): announce, and refuse arming-dependent checks, above an MS5611 TEMP of about 80 °C.

R23 firmware rule 10, bring-up configuration (R23-MCU-01): program and read back these option bytes: BOOT_ADD0 = 0x0800, IWDG1_SW software start, BOR_LEV (state the level, DS12110 Table 126 p217), SWAP_BANK = 0, IO_HSLV = 0, and the RDP level. Also: LDO supply (never bypass), with VOS matched to 200 MHz (Table 122); HSEBYP = 0, a bounded HSE-ready wait, and CSSHSEON with HSI fallback and safety-timer rescaling (FMEA F-2); PLL limits per Table 147; USB VBUS sensing off with a B-session override (PA9 NC). The RM0433 items are an Inference until RM0433 is read.

R23 firmware rule 11, bring-up facts (R23-DOCS_BINDING-03): U5 MS5611 on I2C1 PB8 / PB9 at 0x77 (PS high, CSB low), with R12 / R13 4.7 kΩ pull-ups. IMU_CS (PB7, R11) and QSPI_NCS (PB6, R10) idle high: write the ODR high before switching to output / AF. Scales: PA6 = VLOGIC / 11, PB1 = CAM_5V / 11, PC0 / PC5 = node / 11.2. The PA6 trip from rule 8, and a PA4 settling time to qualify on the bench.

R23 firmware rule 12, clocks (R23-ROUTING-01): avoid SPI3, QSPI and timer clocks with an integer harmonic within ±1.023 MHz of 1575.42 MHz (25 and 75 MHz, for example). This is an Inference until the installed GNSS check has run.

R23 firmware rule 13, IMU (R23-MCU-03): FS_XL_HG code 010 is 3.904 mg/LSB on all three parts and clips at ±80 g on the LSM6DSV80X, so 001 / 010 serve all three. Never use ST's ism6hg256x driver's 256 g enum (0x3 is reserved in DS15034 Table 150).
r10_firmware_obligations_note: R10 text, carried verbatim (R10 pin names, LQFP pin numbers and DB125 terminals); r11_obligation_deltas overrides each obligation it names

r11_obligation_deltas.r11: Camera UART is UART4 AF8: CAM_MCU_TX PB9 (ball A4), CAM_MCU_RX PB8 (ball B4), no flow control (D-R11-49), not UART7 PE8 / PE7. PB9 is a ROM-loader pin (I2C1_SDA, open drain): stageC1b.md section 8.4 case; drive PB9 push-pull only after the UART4 binding.

PE11 / PE12 (loader SPI4) are NC on R11. Camera EN is PC14 (CAM_PWR_EN, ball A1), held low by R431 100 k while PC14 is an input; camera OE is PC15 (ball B1), held low by R102 10 k. New loader members: PA15 (SPI3_NSS) carries SERVO2_MCU (R155 holds it low) and PB9 carries CAM_MCU_TX (stageC1b.md section 8.4).

EXTI map on R11: CAM_FAULT_N PC13 (EXTI13, EXTI15_10), USB_FAULT_N PD10 (EXTI10, EXTI15_10), LOGIC_SOURCE_ST PA4 (EXTI4), BAT_FAULT_N PA5 (EXTI5), IMU_INT1 PD6 (EXTI6, ball C6; D-R11-81), VBUS_SENSE PC8 (EXTI8). Every interrupt net has its own line number (4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 13), so each SYSCFG_EXTICR field selects one port (PA for 4 / 5, PD for 6 / 10, PC for 8 / 13); lines 5 / 6 / 8 share the EXTI9_5 vector and 10 / 13 the EXTI15_10 vector, so each handler checks its pending bit. IMU_INT1 is no longer on EXTI1 (R10) and no longer on PD5 (D-R11-49), which shared line 5 with PA5 (D-R11-77, closed by D-R11-81). PC13 is used on R11 (it was NC); PD5 is NC.

PE3 carries IMU_CS on R11 (ball B3), so it is no longer an analog sentinel; the sentinels are PE5 / PE6 / PC4. PA15 carries SERVO2_MCU (TIM2_CH1 AF1): it resets as JTDI with its internal pull-up, which against R155 10 k gives at most 0.83 V on the line until firmware selects TIM2 (stageC1b.md section 8.4, Calculation with a 30 k minimum pull-up, Inference); configure PA15 early, as R10 required for the no-net PA15.

Servo timers on R11: SERVO1 PB7 TIM4_CH2 AF2 (ball A5), SERVO2 PA15 TIM2_CH1 AF1 (A8), SERVO3 PA0 TIM5_CH1 AF2 (G2), SERVO4 PA1 TIM5_CH2 AF2 (H2): three timers, so the neutral-first-pulse and 50 ms rules apply to each timer start.

R11 connectors (D-R11-05): J122 / J400 / J410 / J420 / J440 / J9 are latching JST GH (J9 six-pin: 1-2 CAM_5V, 3-4 GND, 5 RXI, 6 TXO); J1 (battery) and J121 (igniter) are hand-soldered AWG 20 wire pads. The DB125 text is R10 only.

The buzzer gate is driven by PE8 (BUZZ_DRV, ball J5) through R162, initialised low; PC14 now drives CAM_PWR_EN (U402 EN, R431 100 k; at most 0.04 mA, Calculation in pin_table.tsv), still a VBAT-domain pin at 3 mA / 2 MHz.
Buzzer on PE8, not PC14. PC13 carries CAM_FAULT_N (input). PE0 and PE10 stay NC.
Camera start-up: RX PB8 pull-up and TX PB9 idle high before OE (PC15) goes high.
CAM_5V_SENSE is PC2_C (ball E2), ADC3_INP0 (the analog-only _C pad), not PB1 ADC12_INP5; ADC3 also carries the VBAT/4 bridge reading. PB1 carries LED_RED.
LEDs: LED_RED PB1 (ball K4), LED_YEL PD2 (ball B7).
LSE: PC14 (OSC32_IN) now drives CAM_PWR_EN; keep RCC_BDCR.LSEON = 0 as on R10.

CAM_5V_SENSE moved to PC2_C, an analog-only switch pad. Single fault R105 open: the pin is pulled to CAM_5V (nominal 5.456 V) through R104 10 kOhm, as R10's PB1 case, which R10 recorded above its 4.0 V TT_u limit with no firmware mitigation. The PC2_C absolute maximum was not read from DS12110 in D-R11-81's session (ST's PDF could not be fetched); taking it as R10's 4.0 V class is an Inference, under which the fault exceeds it as on R10 (injection through 10 kOhm at most about 0.2 mA, Inference). Owner item, no design change (D-R11-81).
PE3 is IMU_CS: synchronous trace (TRACED0 on PE3) would also drive the IMU chip select; the trace prohibition stands. The lock list is unchanged (PC1, PE4).

Rule 3 on R11: QSPI_IO2 is PE2 (ball A3) and PE4 is ball C3, with PE3 / IMU_CS (B3) between them; a BGA bridge cannot be seen, so the visual "U1 pins 1-5" inspection becomes X-ray of U1, and the U3.3-to-R127.1 meter check stays. The cold-screen toggle list is the buzzer PE8 (not PC14) and the servo PWM.
The R10 second-barrel coordinates are R10 records; R11 gate barrels are in the R11 board and S-8 data.

The R91.1 / U1.28 second vias are R10 records. On R11 PA4 (LOGIC_SOURCE_ST, ball G3) has two single-via points, its dog-bone (21.60, 28.80) and its In3-to-B.Cu via (14.65, 39.90) (D-R11-45, D-R11-48, single_open_exceptions): an open leaves PA4 floating, so rule 5 (PC1 only while PA4 reads low) stays an extra barrier, not a guarantee.
EXTI5 is BAT_FAULT_N's alone on R11 (IMU_INT1 is on EXTI6, D-R11-81); rule 7 stands as R10.

U5 (MS5611) is on I2C2, PB10 SCL (ball J7) / PB11 SDA (ball K7), AF4 (D-R11-41; the nets keep the names I2C1_SCL / I2C1_SDA); PB10 / PB11 are loader USART3 pins (stageC1b.md section 7). IMU_CS is PE3 (ball B3). CAM_5V scale: PC2_C = CAM_5V / 11.

r11_firmware_rules: An R11 binding changes the TIM, UART, ADC and EXTI assignments together (stageC1b.md section 8.2); R10 firmware cannot run on R11.

EXTI lines on R11 (D-R11-81): 4 PA4 LOGIC_SOURCE_ST, 5 PA5 BAT_FAULT_N, 6 PD6 IMU_INT1, 8 PC8 VBUS_SENSE, 10 PD10 USB_FAULT_N, 13 PC13 CAM_FAULT_N; one port per line in SYSCFG_EXTICR (Inference on RM0433, not re-read: ST's PDF could not be fetched in that session).
